name: FALSE
description: FALSE returns the logical value FALSE. It takes no arguments and is equivalent to typing the literal FALSE into a cell.

basicExample.explanation: The function evaluates to the logical constant FALSE with no input needed.

advancedExamples.title: Use inside a condition
advancedExamples.scenario: Force the false branch of an IF
advancedExamples.explanation: Because FALSE() is logical FALSE, the IF returns its value_if_false.

advancedExamples.title: Explicit boolean in a check
advancedExamples.scenario: Compare a cell to a target
advancedExamples.explanation: Returns the explicit TRUE/FALSE constants instead of relying on implicit coercion.

howItWorks: FALSE is a function wrapper around the FALSE logical constant. It performs no computation and accepts no arguments; it is provided for compatibility and explicit boolean building.

howToSteps.name: Use the result
howToSteps.text: Reference it in logical tests like IF or AND.

limitations: Takes no arguments; supplying any returns #VALUE!.
Mostly redundant because the literal FALSE works the same in formulas.
Stored as a logical value, not the text "FALSE".

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: FALSE works identically in Google Sheets with no arguments.

faq.question: Is FALSE() different from typing FALSE?
faq.answer: No, =FALSE() and the constant FALSE behave the same in calculations.

faq.question: Can FALSE take arguments?
faq.answer: No; it returns #VALUE! if you supply any.
